news.headline: Gap in counting Indians left epistemic void: ex-Registrar General, Census Commissioner Chandramouli
news.story_lead: Gap in counting Indians left epistemic void: ex-Registrar General, Census Commissioner Chandramouli Chandramouli warns that a single identity authority could become an “overly powerful data-holder”, raising concerns A sixteen-year gap in counting Indians has left the country in an “epistemic void”, and Census 2027 must close it without turning a head count into a citizenship test, says former Registrar General and Census Commissioner C Chandramouli in his new book, Counting a Nation . “A democracy cannot govern what it cannot see,” Chandramouli writes, arguing that budgets, urban plans and welfare schemes now rest on decade-old figures and modelled estimates. The last census, in 2011, counted 1.21 billion people.
news.full_article_text: Gap in counting Indians left epistemic void: ex-Registrar General, Census Commissioner Chandramouli Chandramouli warns that a single identity authority could become an “overly powerful data-holder”, raising concerns A sixteen-year gap in counting Indians has left the country in an “epistemic void”, and Census 2027 must close it without turning a head count into a citizenship test, says former Registrar General and Census Commissioner C Chandramouli in his new book, Counting a Nation . “A democracy cannot govern what it cannot see,” Chandramouli writes, arguing that budgets, urban plans and welfare schemes now rest on decade-old figures and modelled estimates. The last census, in 2011, counted 1.21 billion people. Census 2021 was postponed because of the Covid-19 pandemic. The book notes that enumeration ran every decade from 1881, even through the 1918-19 influenza pandemic and the Second World War. Chandramouli warns that a single identity authority could become an “overly powerful data-holder”, raising concerns of surveillance and profiling. He notes that the Citizenship (Amendment) Act and the National Register of Citizens have made any link between counting and citizenship politically charged. That is why the book treats 2027 as more than a routine exercise. It argues that for the first time the census will trigger a constitutionally mandated redistribution of political power, and that it is expected to run alongside an update of the National Population Register (NPR). The UN estimated India’s population at 1.43 billion in 2023, which is 220 million, or about 18%, above the 2011 count. Without a census, the book says, these remain modelled estimates. Census 2011 listed 7,935 towns, of which 3,894 were census towns. Scholars now estimate more than 10,000 urban settlements, so over a fifth of them are missing from official records. The 2011 census counted 450 million migrants, or 37% of the population. Estimates now run well above 600 million, a rise of at least a third, but there is no authoritative figure. The book says any delay in the census postpones the women’s quota with it, and undercounts or regional imbalances now carry “constitutional significance” because they can shift seats between and within states. It says women have often been more difficult to count. The book points to the long history of missing girls. “The challenge of Census 2027 is not merely to count more efficiently, but to count more justly,” the book says. Chandramouli says caste enumeration cannot be left to administrative improvisation, because the Census Act of 1948 was framed for a confidential demographic count and not for classifying caste groups. He recalls the Socio-Economic and Caste Census of 2011, run outside the census framework, which showed the risks of unclear classification and disputes over names. He proposes a dedicated Caste Enumeration Act, with the National Commission for Backward Classes validating self-declared responses.

news.headline: ED summons Rajya Sabha member Satnam Singh Sandhu in foreign exchange violations case
news.story_lead: ED summons Rajya Sabha member Satnam Singh Sandhu in foreign exchange violations case Sandhu has been asked to appear to verify the nature and purpose of funds from a company under investigation The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has issued a summons to Rajya Sabha member Satnam Singh Sandhu in connection with a foreign exchange violation, people familiar with the development said on Friday. Sandhu, who is Chancellor of Chandigarh University, has been asked to appear before the agency to verify the nature and purpose of certain funds from a company under investigation in a Ponzi scheme, an officer said, requesting anonymity. There was no immediate response from Sandhu.
news.full_article_text: ED summons Rajya Sabha member Satnam Singh Sandhu in foreign exchange violations case Sandhu has been asked to appear to verify the nature and purpose of funds from a company under investigation The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has issued a summons to Rajya Sabha member Satnam Singh Sandhu in connection with a foreign exchange violation, people familiar with the development said on Friday. Sandhu, who is Chancellor of Chandigarh University, has been asked to appear before the agency to verify the nature and purpose of certain funds from a company under investigation in a Ponzi scheme, an officer said, requesting anonymity. There was no immediate response from Sandhu. The officer added that ED’s Jalandhar Zonal office issued the summons without specifying the date for appearance. “He has been summoned to verify the nature and purpose of some transactions. He is not summoned for any direct role in any money laundering case,” the officer said. The company and its CEO are alleged to have orchestrated a multi-thousand-crore ‘cloud particle scam’ wherein money of investors was siphoned off for personal gains. In a statement in February, the ED said that the “underlying business of cloud particle, based on the Sale and Lease Back model (SLB model), was found substantively non-existent and grossly overstated to cheat the investors”. “It is also revealed that no rental amount, or an insignificant amount, is received from the data centre clients as the entire business of Vuenow group was found to be only a money rotation scheme,” ED said. The ED said that money collected from the investors in lieu of sale of cloud particles was found to be ₹ 3700 crore (approx), out of which ₹ 1800 crore (approx) was returned to investors in the form of rent, and the remaining Proceeds of Crime were utilised for purposes other than business. - Enforcement Directorate

### Cheetah Population Milestone in India

In a notable achievement for wildlife conservation, a female cheetah originally translocated from Botswana has given birth to four cubs in the wild in India. The addition of these four newborn cubs brings India's overall cheetah population to 62.

### Key Highlights

- **Mother's Origin:** Botswana
- **Newborn Cubs:** 4 cubs born in natural wild conditions
- **Updated National Total:** 62 cheetahs
- **Significance:** Successful mating and cub birth in the wild reflect positive acclimatization of translocated African cheetahs to Indian forest ecosystems.

### Context of Reintroduction

Under Project Cheetah, India has been importing cheetahs from African countries, including Namibia, South Africa, and Botswana, to restore the predator's ecological role in Indian grasslands and open forest systems.
news.background_context: India officially declared the cheetah extinct within its borders in 1952. The Government of India subsequently launched Project Cheetah to reintroduce the species by translocating specimens from African nations.

* **प्रक्रियात्मक स्थिति:** यह मामला न्यायालय की सामान्य कार्यसूची और रजिस्ट्री प्रक्रिया के तहत अपने तय क्रम में सुना जाएगा।

news.headline: Supreme Court Rejects Tamil Nadu's Plea Seeking Immediate Release of Cauvery Water Backlog
news.story_lead: The Supreme Court of India has dismissed an application filed by Tamil Nadu seeking directions to Karnataka for the immediate release of an alleged backlog of 11.719 thousand million cubic feet (TMC) of Cauvery water. A bench comprising Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh rejected the plea, remarking that the state was spending excessive resources on legal battles while a fresh application was also slated for dismissal. The judgment upholds reliance on existing statutory bodies like the Cauvery Water Management Authority during distress periods.
news.full_article_text:
### Cauvery Water Sharing Dispute: Supreme Court Dismissal

The Supreme Court of India dismissed a petition filed by the Tamil Nadu government seeking an order for Karnataka to release 1.3 thousand million cubic feet (TMC) of water per day over a 10-day period at the Billigundulu measuring station to compensate for an alleged deficit in Cauvery river flows.

#### Key Directives and Judicial Observations
- **Bench Composition:** The order was passed by a bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh.
- **Judicial Remarks:** Justice Nath remarked that Tamil Nadu appeared to have abundant resources being spent on repeated litigation in the decades-old inter-state river dispute.
- **Dismissal of Parallel Application:** Noting that Tamil Nadu had moved another application on the same day seeking fresh directions, the court expressed its inclination to dismiss it as well, prompting the state's legal counsel to request an adjournment.

#### Submissions by Tamil Nadu
- **Calculated Shortfall:** Tamil Nadu pegged the accumulated shortfall in water flows at Billigundulu at 11.719 TMC up to October 6.
- **Reservoir Levels:** Tamil Nadu asserted that Karnataka maintained a combined reservoir storage of roughly 49 TMC, which it argued was sufficient to satisfy downstream obligations even in a distress year.
- **Regulatory Inaction Allegation:** The state argued that the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) and the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) failed to compel Karnataka to clear the deficit during their regular fortnightly meetings.

#### Arguments Presented by Karnataka
- **Drought Conditions:** Karnataka opposed the application, stating that multiple districts in the state were suffering from drought, forcing cuts in local irrigation allocations.
- **Institutional Mandate:** Karnataka maintained that the water-sharing framework governed by the CWMA and CWRC was functioning appropriately and did not require extrajudicial intervention.

#### Baseline Allocation Rules
- **Normal Allocation:** According to the Supreme Court's landmark judgment, Karnataka must release 177 TMC of Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu at Billigundulu in a standard water year.
- **Distress Principle:** During low-rainfall years, allocations are reduced proportionately for both upper and lower riparian states.

hindi_translation.story_lead: सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने तमिलनाडु की उस याचिका को खारिज कर दिया है जिसमें कर्नाटक को कावेरी नदी के कथित 11.719 टीएमसी (हजार मिलियन क्यूबिक फीट) के बकाया पानी को तुरंत छोड़ने का निर्देश देने की मांग की गई थी। न्यायमूर्ति विक्रम नाथ और न्यायमूर्ति अपरेश कुमार सिंह की पीठ ने याचिका खारिज करते हुए टिप्पणी की कि राज्य बार-बार की कानूनी लड़ाइयों पर बहुत अधिक संसाधन खर्च कर रहा है। अदालत ने एक नई याचिका पर भी सुनवाई से इनकार किया।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### कावेरी जल बंटवारा विवाद: सुप्रीम कोर्ट द्वारा याचिका खारिज

भारत के सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने तमिलनाडु सरकार द्वारा दायर उस याचिका को खारिज कर दिया है जिसमें कावेरी नदी के पानी में कथित घाटे की भरपाई के लिए बिलिगुंडलू मापन स्टेशन पर 10 दिनों के लिए प्रतिदिन 1.3 हजार मिलियन क्यूबिक फीट (TMC) पानी छोड़ने का आदेश कर्नाटक को देने की मांग की गई थी।

#### मुख्य निर्देश और अदालती टिप्पणियां
- **पीठ का गठन:** यह आदेश न्यायमूर्ति विक्रम नाथ और न्यायमूर्ति अपरेश कुमार सिंह की पीठ ने दिया।
- **न्यायिक टिप्पणी:** न्यायमूर्ति नाथ ने टिप्पणी की कि तमिलनाडु इस दशकों पुराने अंतर-राज्यीय नदी जल विवाद में बार-बार याचिकाएं दाखिल करके वकीलों पर अत्यधिक धन खर्च कर रहा है।
- **दूसरी याचिका पर रुख:** जब अदालत ने पाया कि तमिलनाडु ने उसी दिन एक और नई याचिका दायर की है, तो उसने उसे भी खारिज करने का संकेत दिया, जिसके बाद राज्य के वकील ने स्थगन का अनुरोध किया।

#### तमिलनाडु द्वारा प्रस्तुत तर्क
- **जल घाटे का दावा:** तमिलनाडु ने 6 अक्टूबर तक बिलिगुंडलू सीमा मापन स्टेशन पर 11.719 टीएमसी के कुल संचित घाटे का दावा किया।
- **जलाशय भंडारण क्षमता:** तमिलनाडु का तर्क था कि कर्नाटक के पास उसके जलाशयों में लगभग 49 टीएमसी का संयुक्त भंडारण मौजूद है, जो संकट के वर्ष में भी निचले तटवर्ती राज्य की जरूरतों को पूरा करने के लिए पर्याप्त है।
- **प्राधिकरण पर आरोप:** राज्य का आरोप था कि कावेरी जल प्रबंधन प्राधिकरण (CWMA) और कावेरी जल नियमन समिति (CWRC) अपनी पाक्षिक बैठकों के दौरान कर्नाटक से बकाया पानी जारी करवाने में विफल रहे।

#### कर्नाटक द्वारा प्रस्तुत तर्क
- **सूखे की स्थिति:** कर्नाटक ने याचिका का विरोध करते हुए कहा कि राज्य के कई जिले गंभीर सूखे का सामना कर रहे हैं, जिससे स्थानीय सिंचाई आवंटन में कटौती करनी पड़ी है।
- **वैधानिक निकायों की भूमिका:** कर्नाटक ने बनाए रखा कि CWMA और CWRC के तहत जल-बंटवारा तंत्र पहले से सक्रिय रूप से कार्य कर रहा है और इसमें अतिरिक्त न्यायिक हस्तक्षेप की आवश्यकता नहीं है।

#### जल-बंटवारे के मूल नियम
- **सामान्य वर्ष का आवंटन:** सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के अंतिम फैसले के तहत, सामान्य जल वर्ष में कर्नाटक को बिलिगुंडलू में तमिलनाडु के लिए 177 टीएमसी कावेरी जल छोड़ना अनिवार्य है।
- **संकट वर्ष का नियम:** कम वर्षा वाले वर्षों में, दोनों ऊपरी और निचले राज्यों के बीच आनुपातिक रूप से आवंटन कम किया जाता है।

### सौर ऊर्जा जीएसटी पर उच्चतम न्यायालय का निर्णय

news.headline: Govt proposes major CSR rule changes, seeks to include mental health, clean energy, PM internship scheme
news.story_lead: Govt proposes major CSR rule changes, seeks to include mental health, clean energy, PM internship scheme Govt proposes new CSR rules: adds mental health, clean energy & internships, while banning one-off events & product freebies, plus stricter NGO oversight. The government has proposed amendments to corporate social responsibility norms, including allowing initiatives in mental health, career counselling, the PM Internship Scheme and clean energy as eligible activities under the companies law. Besides, one-off events, financing of government schemes, corpus fund contributions and in-kind contributions of a company's own products, other than immediate disaster relief, are proposed to be excluded from the CSR ambit.
news.full_article_text: Govt proposes major CSR rule changes, seeks to include mental health, clean energy, PM internship scheme Govt proposes new CSR rules: adds mental health, clean energy & internships, while banning one-off events & product freebies, plus stricter NGO oversight. The government has proposed amendments to corporate social responsibility norms, including allowing initiatives in mental health, career counselling, the PM Internship Scheme and clean energy as eligible activities under the companies law. Besides, one-off events, financing of government schemes, corpus fund contributions and in-kind contributions of a company's own products, other than immediate disaster relief, are proposed to be excluded from the CSR ambit. A certain class of profitable companies are required to shell out at least two per cent of their three-year average annual profit towards Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) activities in a financial year. The corporate affairs ministry has proposed amendments to the Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility Policy) Rules, as well as Schedule VII, which provides a broad list of areas where activities can be eligible under the CSR framework. To expand the scope of CSR activities, the ministry has mooted inclusion of mental health, telemedicine, career counselling, the PM Internship Scheme, clean energy and waste management, including e-waste management, under Schedule VII. Also, animal welfare, marine conservation and sports infrastructure are to be included. Also read: Who is holding the soul of your organisation? The ministry's proposed amendments also seek to put in place a stronger oversight mechanism for implementing agencies wherein the registration of an agency can be cancelled, and once done, there will be a three-year ban on re-registration for the particular agency. Among other amendments, the ministry has proposed that international organisations headquartered in India can be eligible for functioning as CSR implementing agencies. As per the proposed changes, all CSR-mandated companies may commission independent impact assessments. Also read: Fadnavis flags malnutrition in Mumbai slums, calls for targeted CSR interventions Amit Agarwal, Senior Partner at advisory firm Nangia & Co LLP, said the proposed amendments aim to marry the actual spend with the objectives of the CSR framework. "CSR will increasingly be judged not by how much is spent, but by what it achieves on the ground. "... distributing one's own products free of cost has often worked more as brand promotion than as social responsibility. The exclusions draw a clear line between genuine impact and freebies, events or idle corpus funds," he said. In a public notice, the ministry said it has reviewed the existing CSR ecosystem. "... to further strengthen business involvement in CSR, suggestions were invited from various stakeholders, so that the ministry could facilitate businesses to be even more socially, economically, and environmentally responsible. "Multiple suggestions were received from various stakeholders to propose various changes in the CSR framework," it said. Also read: Why disability needs to move beyond CSR The ministry has sought stakeholders' comments on the proposed amendments to the rules till December 11. Anjali Malhotra, Partner - Regulatory at consultancy Nangia Global, said the proposed measures are expected to strengthen regulatory oversight, promote greater transparency and accountability in the allocation and utilisation of CSR funds.

The 21-year-old man accused of attacking a Class 10 student with a chainsaw at Zilla Parishad High School in Rapthadu, Andhra Pradesh’s Anantapur district, was discharged from the Kurnool Government General Hospital, police said on Thursday. Doctors said on Wednesday that Hemanth alias Dummu, who was shot at by police while allegedly attempting to escape custody, was discharged following improvement in his health condition.
news.full_article_text: Man accused in Andhra chainsaw attack discharged from hospital, girl shows signs of recovery The 21-year-old accused in the chainsaw attack on a Class 10 girl in Andhra Pradesh was discharged from hospital and taken back to jail after his health improved. The 21-year-old man accused of attacking a Class 10 student with a chainsaw at Zilla Parishad High School in Rapthadu, Andhra Pradesh’s Anantapur district, was discharged from the Kurnool Government General Hospital, police said on Thursday. Doctors said on Wednesday that Hemanth alias Dummu, who was shot at by police while allegedly attempting to escape custody, was discharged following improvement in his health condition. “He responded well to treatment and his health parameters were now normal. His blood pressure, pulse rate and electrocardiogram (ECG) reports were all within normal limits, indicating that he had recovered sufficiently,” Kurnool hospital superintendent Dr K Venkateshwarlu said. The doctors submitted their medical report to the judge of the local court in the afternoon, following which the police took Hemanth back to Anantapur, where he was lodged in Reddipalli jail, a police officer said. Hemanth had allegedly entered the school premises carrying a chainsaw and attacked the student on October 31. Doctors at Manipal Hospital in Bengaluru informed the state government that the girl, who suffered serious injuries, was showing significant signs of recovery. news.headline: Scientists flooded GTA’s Los Santos to simulate rising seas
news.story_lead: Scientists flooded GTA’s Los Santos to simulate rising seas They used a fan-built 3D model of the map, and pinned it to coordinates with 11 control points and set the sea level from 31 shoreline points The water reached Vespucci’s canals first. Then the Port of South Los Santos stopped working, followed by the gasworks and the sewage plant. Nobody in a stolen car caused any of this.
news.full_article_text: Scientists flooded GTA’s Los Santos to simulate rising seas They used a fan-built 3D model of the map, and pinned it to coordinates with 11 control points and set the sea level from 31 shoreline points The water reached Vespucci’s canals first. Then the Port of South Los Santos stopped working, followed by the gasworks and the sewage plant. Nobody in a stolen car caused any of this. The sea simply came in. That’s Los Santos, the sunbathed in-game version of Los Angeles of Grand Theft Auto V, in the face of a rising seas scenario modelled by Paul Nörenberg and Hugues Lantuit of the University of Potsdam and the Alfred Wegener Institute. Their paper coincides with the launch of the GTA VI video game. Los Santos, they say, serves as an ideal case study because it faithfully replicates the real Los Angeles, thereby enabling a direct comparison of simulated flood outcomes. The scientists are working with two Representative Concentration Pathway (RCP) scenarios from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Fifth Assessment Report (AR5). The researchers used these scenarios to simulate the consequences of any future sea-level rise and demonstrate the exact ways the city in GTA V would change. The research notes that under the RCP 8.5 scenario with storm surges, combined sea levels are projected to reach 5.18 m by 2300, with the model showing 5.1 % of the mapped land area inundated; for a 2500 scenario with projected sea levels of 8.22 mm, this increases to 6.5 % modelled inundation, which places the port, wastewater infrastructure, and coastal energy facilities at risk. Under the RCP 2.6 mitigation scenario, the model shows 2.2 % of land area inundated at 2300 with storm surge, with no major infrastructure affected. “Many games have now advanced graphically to such an extent that they can reproduce real-world locations almost true to life,” says Paul Nörenberg, lead author of the study. Grand Theft Auto V (GTA V) is one of those games: it takes players to the fictional city of Los Santos. “The city is a near-exact replica of the real-life Los Angeles, with all its famous landmarks, neighbourhoods as well as urban and coastal features.” In 2017, four scientific modelling teams, from the Netherlands, US, Japan and Austria, coordinated through the Integrated Assessment Modeling Consortium (IAMC) to create four scenarios, which the United Nations’ IPCC published. Rockstar doesn’t release any raw terrain data. The scientists used a fan-built 3D model of the map, pinned it to coordinates with 11 control points and set the sea level from 31 shoreline points. This was checked by flying an in-game helicopter along the coastline. The height was calibrated against the game’s Mount Chiliad. They then simulated the IPCC scenarios for the years 2100, 2300 and 2500—each topped with a 1.59-metre storm surge, the highest Los Angeles has ever recorded. When the scientists overlaid the simulation data over real maps and flood studies for Los Angeles, the same districts in reality also stood most exposed. Vespucci floods like Venice Beach might, Chumash like Malibu, and the Port of South Los Santos is as vulnerable as the Port of LA. Rockstar Games, the developer, copied the city closely enough to inadvertently replicate its weak spots. Rockstar Games says GTA V is the second best-selling video game of all time, with more than 225 million copies sold in the last decade. There is a large community of players familiar with Los Santos. “If this familiar, personally explored virtual landscape changes, players can engage with the effects of climate change on an emotional level,” notes Nörenberg. “This can bridge a gap in a way that conventional visualisations, such as models or maps, struggle to achieve.” The scientists agree this isn’t without caveats. “We recommend the approach as a template for geoscience communication using open-world video game environments, with the explicit caveat that the static inundation model and its limitations must be communicated transparently to every audience, and that the 2300 and 2500 horizons remain the weakest part of the scenario set,” they say. A commercial video game is built for storytelling and action, not exactly for rigorous scientific modelling. The terrain is often simplified and static water levels often cannot replicate finer natural nuances such as coastal erosion, drainage systems, or shifting weather patterns. The template, may have given scientists a new avenue. As game studios spend billions building realistic virtual twins of real cities, scientists now have a real-world utility for those maps. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Vishal Mathur Vishal Mathur is Technology Editor for Hindustan Times. When not making sense of technology, he often searches for an elusive analog space in a digital world.

District collectors have been directed to review non-essential new projects, including parks, beautification works, new office and administrative buildings, cement roads, drains and other works involving substantial water consumption, and take steps to temporarily defer them in accordance with prescribed procedures. Funds available for such deferred projects will be reviewed and reallocated to priority drought-relief works in the affected talukas, the GR said, adding that the exercise of reallocation must be completed by December 31. The government has clarified that ongoing projects should not be stopped indiscriminately. Authorities must take decisions on a case-by-case basis after considering contractual obligations, public safety, the stage of work, expenditure already incurred and possible compensation or financial liabilities, it said. Essential works directly related to drinking water availability, strengthening existing water sources, creating necessary new sources, providing water and fodder for livestock, water conservation, irrigation, public health and emergency requirements have been exempted from the temporary suspension, subject to applicable rules and approvals. The GR also gives priority to completing incomplete pipelines, pumps, electricity connections, storage tanks and distribution systems required to transport water from existing sources to scarcity-hit villages. "Projects that can be completed during the current scarcity period and provide immediate access to water must receive priority. New projects that cannot normally be completed within the current financial year should not be sanctioned under the special priority framework," it said. In exceptional cases, essential drinking water, livestock water or water-source creation projects may be considered even if they extend beyond the current financial year. However, the additional financial liability for 2027-28 must not exceed 10 per cent of the approved District Annual Plan outlay for 2026-27. District collectors have been asked to convene meetings of district-level officials within seven days of the issuance of the GR and prepare an integrated taluka-wise and project-wise action plan within 15 days. The government has also provided for expedited approval of urgent drought-relief measures. If convening a District Planning Committee meeting would delay an essential intervention, the collector can submit a proposal to the guardian minister, who heads the committee, for approval, subject to ratification at its subsequent meeting. Collectors will have to review the progress of approved works and submit reports on fund allocation, expenditure and physical progress to the Planning and Finance departments by the 10th of every month. The GR also mandates the publication of details of sanctioned works, funds, expenditure and progress on district collectorate websites or government portals. The provisions will apply to the 304 drought-hit talukas and any additional talukas subsequently declared drought-affected or facing scarcity. The order will remain applicable for the 2026-27 financial year.

news.full_article_text: Resignation not admission of wrongdoing, I am innocent: Justice Varma tells Lok Sabha secretariat New Delhi, Justice Yashwant Varma has asserted that he is innocent of the allegations relating to the discovery of burnt currency notes at his official residence and that his resignation as a high court judge should not be construed as an acknowledgement or admission of any wrongdoing or of the findings against him. In a letter to Lok Sabha Secretary General Utpal Kumar Singh on September 10 – which was circulated among MPs on Thursday – Varma also contended that proceedings for his removal had become infructuous following his resignation on April 9, and any attempt to remove him from office would be without constitutional foundation. Citing Article 217 of the Constitution and a 1978 Constitution Bench judgment of the Supreme Court in 'Union of India vs Gopal Chandra Mishra', he argued that a high court judge's resignation takes effect by its own force and does not require acceptance by the President or any other authority. "Upon my resignation, proceedings directed towards my removal from office did not survive and cannot be continued," he wrote, arguing that the constitutional provisions governing the removal of judges apply to sitting judges and not those who have ceased to hold office. Varma said he had participated in the inquiry before the Judges Inquiry Committee until April 9, when he tendered his resignation to the President with immediate effect. He also referred to objections he had raised over the manner in which the inquiry was conducted, saying he was reserving his right to challenge the findings. Declining to furnish comments on the committee's report or participate in any further process, he requested that his letter and its enclosures be placed before members of both Houses of Parliament and that the matter be closed. The three-member inquiry committee constituted by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla had found all three charges against Varma proved in its report, tabled in Parliament on August 12. The charges related to his failure to explain the presence, source and ownership of cash found at his official residence, failure to secure and preserve material evidence, and evasive and unsatisfactory explanations during the inquiry. The controversy dates back to March 14, 2025, when burnt bundles of currency notes were found at Varma's official residence here following a fire. news.full_article_text:
### Major Narcotics Interdictions in Tamil Nadu

Central law enforcement agencies executed significant drug busts in Tamil Nadu, sparking widespread political debate regarding state narcotics control. The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) intercepted a vehicle in Madhavaram, Chennai, confiscating 70 kg of heroin valued at ₹140 crore and arresting two individuals. This operation follows a prior DRI raid in Nagapattinam that seized contraband worth ₹270 crore linked to illicit distribution networks.

### Political Allegations and Public Debates

Following the seizures, DMK Chief M.K. Stalin criticized the TVK-led state administration under Chief Minister Vijay, characterizing the state's security situation as severely deteriorated. Drawing parallels to 'Vice City' from the Grand Theft Auto video game franchise, Stalin highlighted issues including rising illicit substance trafficking, alleged criminal misconduct, major robberies, and custodial deaths. He questioned why primary drug seizures were being conducted by federal agencies rather than the 65 state-level special task force teams dedicated to anti-narcotics operations.

AMMK General Secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran also urged the state government to move beyond public awareness campaigns and execute concrete actions against drug networks distributing synthetic and organic narcotics across the state.

### Police Campaign and National Context

In response to public discourse, Tamil Nadu Police released anti-drug informational graphics themed after GTA VI artwork. Titled 'Grand Theft Demolisher' and 'Drive Against Drugs', the communications underscored police actions including digital map tracking of trafficking routes, suspect detentions, and student outreach campaigns.

Concurrently, Prime Minister Narendra Modi utilized the backdrop of the global release of GTA VI—coming 13 years after GTA V in 2013—to highlight India's national development metrics between 2013 and 2026. The 10-slide presentation detailed progress in economic growth, sanitation coverage, solar power capacity, space startups, rural electrification, defense exports, and the decline of internal security challenges in Maoist-affected regions.

केन्द्रीय प्रवर्तन एजेंसियों ने तमिलनाडु में नशीली दवाओं की बड़ी खेप जब्त की, जिससे राज्य में कानून प्रवर्तन पर राजनीतिक चर्चा शुरू हो गई। राजस्व खुफिया निदेशालय (DRI) ने चेन्नई के माधवराम में एक वाहन को रोककर 140 करोड़ रुपये मूल्य की 70 किलोग्राम हेरोइन जब्त की और दो लोगों को गिरफ्तार किया। इससे पहले डीआरआई ने नागपट्टिनम में 270 करोड़ रुपये मूल्य के नशीले पदार्थ जब्त किए थे।

### राजनीतिक आरोप और प्रतिक्रियाएं

डीएमके प्रमुख एम.के. स्टालिन ने टीवीके नेतृत्व वाली राज्य सरकार की आलोचना करते हुए राज्य की कानून-व्यवस्था की स्थिति पर सवाल उठाए। उन्होंने मादक पदार्थों की तस्करी, आपराधिक घटनाओं और हिरासत में मौतों का जिक्र किया। उन्होंने पूछा कि राज्य की 65 विशेष टास्क फोर्स टीमों के बजाय केंद्रीय एजेंसियां ​​ही प्रमुख जब्तियां क्यों कर रही हैं।

वहीं एएमएमके महासचिव टी.टी.वी. दिनकरन ने भी सरकार से केवल जागरूकता अभियानों तक सीमित न रहकर नशीली दवाओं के नेटवर्क के खिलाफ सख्त प्रवर्तन कार्रवाई करने का आग्रह किया।

तमिलनाडु पुलिस ने डिजिटल पोस्टरों के माध्यम से नशीली दवाओं के खिलाफ जागरूकता अभियान चलाया। इन पोस्टरों में मैपिंग के जरिए तस्करी नेटवर्क को ट्रैक करने, गिरफ्तारियों और छात्रों के लिए जागरूकता सत्रों की जानकारी दी गई।

news.story_lead: The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has approached the Supreme Court seeking the recall of its September 28 order that exempted Class VI students from the mandatory three-language policy. The Board submitted that the relaxation affects under 0.2% of Class VI students nationwide and disrupts existing academic arrangements across affiliated institutions.
news.full_article_text:
### CBSE Three-Language Policy & Supreme Court Proceedings

The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has moved an application before the Supreme Court seeking to recall its interim order dated September 28, which had extended exemption from the mandatory three-language policy to Class VI students for the current academic session. Appearing before a bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Additional Solicitor General (ASG) Aishwarya Bhati stated that minor administrative issues required resolution, following which the apex court scheduled the application for hearing in the upcoming week.

According to official enrolment metrics submitted by CBSE, out of more than 2.344 million students enrolled in Class VI across affiliated schools, approximately 99.82% (over 2.340 million) are already studying two native Indian languages. The Board emphasized that the court's relief effectively applies to only 4,186 students nationwide (roughly 0.18%) who are studying two foreign languages across 99 specific institutions.

### Infrastructure and Faculty Availability Data

To counter claims regarding lack of infrastructure, CBSE submitted national school statistics showing that India has 1,466,682 operational schools (CBSE and non-CBSE) catering to 247.21 million students. Of these, 33,017 schools are affiliated with CBSE, enrolling over 27.5 million students from Class I to XII. Within the 99 CBSE schools where 4,186 students pursue two foreign languages, 19,892 students in the same schools are studying two native languages, proving that facilities for teaching native languages are present.

CBSE informed the court that digital textbooks for Class VI across all 22 scheduled Indian languages listed in the Eighth Schedule are published on the NCERT portal, while SCERT resources cover remaining regional choices. On teacher deployment, out of 20,777 CBSE schools evaluated, approximately 93% possess instructors for at least two distinct indigenous languages, and 3,523 schools employ teachers for three or more native languages. The Centre had also created a five-member monitoring panel on September 16, headed by Education Ministry Director Bhagwati Prasad Kalal, alongside members from NCERT, CBSE, KVS, and NVS to oversee implementation.
news.background_context: On September 28, the Supreme Court granted Class VI students exemption from the three-language framework to align them with relief previously extended to Classes VII, VIII, and IX. Parents and students had filed petitions citing mid-year implementation uncertainty, lack of textbooks, and unready teaching infrastructure. CBSE challenged this, stating that affiliated schools have taught two native languages for decades and that mid-session exemptions disrupt established school timetables.

hindi_translation.story_lead: केन्द्रीय माध्यमिक शिक्षा बोर्ड (CBSE) ने उच्चतम न्यायालय का रुख कर 28 सितंबर के उस आदेश को वापस लेने की मांग की है, जिसके तहत कक्षा 6 के छात्रों को अनिवार्य त्रि-भाषा नीति से छूट दी गई थी। बोर्ड ने कहा कि इस छूट का लाभ देश भर में कक्षा 6 के 0.2% से भी कम छात्रों को मिलता है और इससे शैक्षणिक व्यवस्था प्रभावित होती है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### CBSE त्रि-भाषा नीति और सुप्रीम कोर्ट की कार्यवाही

केन्द्रीय माध्यमिक शिक्षा बोर्ड (CBSE) ने सुप्रीम कोर्ट में एक आवेदन दायर कर 28 सितंबर के अपने अंतरिम आदेश को वापस लेने का अनुरोध किया है, जिसने चालू शैक्षणिक वर्ष के लिए कक्षा 6 के छात्रों को अनिवार्य त्रि-भाषा नीति से छूट प्रदान की थी। भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश सूर्य कांत की अध्यक्षता वाली पीठ के समक्ष पेश होते हुए अतिरिक्त सॉलिसिटर जनरल (ASG) ऐश्वर्या भाटी ने कहा कि कुछ प्रशासनिक मुद्दों को सुलझाना आवश्यक है, जिसके बाद अदालत ने आवेदन पर अगले सप्ताह सुनवाई करने पर सहमति व्यक्त की।

बोर्ड द्वारा प्रस्तुत आधिकारिक आंकड़ों के अनुसार, सीबीएसई से संबद्ध स्कूलों में कक्षा 6 में नामांकित 2.344 मिलियन से अधिक छात्रों में से लगभग 99.82% (2.340 मिलियन से अधिक) छात्र पहले से ही दो देशी भारतीय भाषाओं का अध्ययन कर रहे हैं। बोर्ड ने स्पष्ट किया कि अदालत के आदेश का लाभ देश भर में केवल 4,186 छात्रों (लगभग 0.18%) को मिलता है, जो 99 स्कूलों में दो विदेशी भाषाओं की पढ़ाई कर रहे हैं।

### बुनियादी ढांचा और शिक्षकों की उपलब्धता के आंकड़े

संसाधनों की कमी के दावों का खंडन करते हुए CBSE ने राष्ट्रीय आंकड़े पेश किए, जिनके अनुसार भारत में कुल 1,466,682 स्कूल (सीबीएसई और गैर-सीबीएसई) हैं, जिनमें 247.21 मिलियन छात्र पंजीकृत हैं। इनमें से 33,017 स्कूल सीबीएसई से संबद्ध हैं, जिनमें कक्षा 1 से 12 तक 27.5 मिलियन से अधिक छात्र पढ़ते हैं। कक्षा 6 में दो विदेशी भाषाएं पढ़ा रहे 99 स्कूलों में भी 19,892 छात्र दो देशी भाषाओं का अध्ययन कर रहे हैं, जो दर्शाता है कि देशी भाषाओं के शिक्षण की व्यवस्था उपलब्ध है।

बोर्ड ने कोर्ट को बताया कि 8वीं अनुसूची की सभी 22 अनुसूचित भारतीय भाषाओं के लिए कक्षा 6 की डिजिटल पाठ्यपुस्तकें NCERT की वेबसाइट पर उपलब्ध हैं। इसके अलावा, 20,777 सीबीएसई स्कूलों के सर्वेक्षण में लगभग 93% स्कूलों के पास कम से कम दो देशी भाषाओं के शिक्षक उपलब्ध हैं और 3,523 स्कूलों में तीन या अधिक देशी भाषाओं के शिक्षक तैनात हैं। केंद्र सरकार ने 16 सितंबर को शिक्षा मंत्रालय के निदेशक भगवती प्रसाद कलाल की अध्यक्षता में 5 सदस्यीय समिति का भी गठन किया था।
hindi_translation.background_context: सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने 28 सितंबर को कक्षा 6 के छात्रों को त्रि-भाषा नीति से छूट दी थी ताकि उन्हें कक्षा 7, 8 और 9 के छात्रों के समान राहत मिल सके। छात्रों और अभिभावकों ने सत्र के मध्य में नीति लागू करने, पुस्तकों और शिक्षकों की कमी का हवाला देते हुए याचिकाएं दायर की थीं। CBSE ने इसका विरोध करते हुए कहा कि स्कूल दशकों से दो देशी भाषाएं पढ़ा रहे हैं और सत्र के बीच में छूट से शैक्षणिक व्यवस्था में अनिश्चितता पैदा होती है।
bullet_points: CBSE ने कक्षा 6 के छात्रों को त्रि-भाषा नीति से मिली छूट को वापस लेने के लिए सुप्रीम कोर्ट में याचिका दायर की।
आंकड़ों के अनुसार, 99.82% (23.4 लाख से अधिक) छात्र पहले से ही दो देशी भारतीय भाषाएं पढ़ रहे हैं।
छूट का प्रभाव केवल 99 स्कूलों के 4,186 छात्रों (0.18%) पर पड़ता है जो विदेशी भाषाएं पढ़ रहे हैं।
चालू शैक्षणिक सत्र में कक्षा 6 के लगभग 45,000 छात्रों ने दो देशी भाषाओं का विकल्प चुना।
8वीं अनुसूची की सभी 22 अनुसूचित भाषाओं के लिए कक्षा 6 की पुस्तकें NCERT की वेबसाइट पर उपलब्ध हैं।
सर्वेक्षण किए गए 20,777 सीबीएसई स्कूलों में से 93% में कम से कम दो देशी भाषाओं के शिक्षक मौजूद हैं।
शिक्षा मंत्रालय के निदेशक भगवती प्रसाद कलाल की अध्यक्षता में 5 सदस्यीय समिति नीति के कार्यान्वयन की निगरानी कर रही है।
CJI सूर्य कांत की अध्यक्षता वाली पीठ सीबीएसई के आवेदन पर अगले सप्ताह सुनवाई करने के लिए सहमत हुई।
